newsitem.title: INDIA: Chidambaram bold on reforms, wary on oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Chidambaram bold on reforms, wary on oil prices.

text.p: India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Monday further economic reforms will be announced in the next few days, but dampened expectations of imminent rises in petroleum product prices.

Chidamabaram, speaking on the Business Agenda programme broadcast by Star Plus channel, said new policy measures would be announced before he and Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda left on January 30 to attend a conference in Switzerland.
Deve Gowda told a conference on Monday that some reforms will be announced before he goes to the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, which starts on January 31.
The government will announce its 1997/98 (April-March) budget proposal on February 28.

"We are determined to go through and push reforms. What we need is not less but more reforms," the transcript of Chidambaram's comments, given in a press release by the programme's producers INTV, quoted the finance minister as saying.
"The need is for more restructuring, more liberalisation, more freedom. All this can be done if we take hard decisions and if we take them quickly," the finance minister said.

He said one of those hard decisions was whether to raise state-controlled petroleum product prices to alleviate some of the resulting pressures on domestic oil companies, but he gave no hint that a quick decision in the pipeline.

"It is a difficult question. Do not underestimate the difficulty of raising petroleum prices twice in a year. We took one difficult decision last July (by raising prices) and to ask us to take another within six months is doubly difficult," Chidambaram said.

The finance minister said the government's target of raising 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion) through disinvestment, which earlier this month he admitted would not be hit, was taken from the interim budget presented by the previous Congress Party government last year.
He said he expected an update on the sell-off of equity in state-owned companies by the Disinvestment Committee next month.
Chidambaram said sales of stakes in telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nagam Ltd (VSNL) and Indian Oil Corp (IOC) will help raise revenues.
The government has slated seven percent of VSNL for sale and five percent of IOC.

"I am confident that part of the proceeds will come from VSNL and, or, IOC. I agree disinvestment has an overall impact on the budget exercise but if the proceeds from the rest come in the next fiscal year, it is alright by me," he said.
